alignments.note: Protasis conjunction אִם takes the *If* written for it.
Finite verb with its subject pronoun and auxiliary, headed on the lexical verb (rules 17, 24).
Anarthrous substantival participle takes the supplied determiner *any*, headed on the word carrying the lexeme (rules 46, 31).
The privative מִן keeps the causal function word the ASV writes for it; the negation goes to the negative morpheme standing in the clause (rule 48).

בְּלִי is the negative substantive that *want* realizes (rule 48). Corrected: the *of* is not part of this morpheme's rendering. MACULA tags בְּלִי Ncmsc, so it stands in construct on לְבוּשׁ, and rule 19 gives the chain's own relation to the nomen rectum — exactly as `כָּל־עֵץ` → *any kind of tree* gives *of tree* to its rectum and forbids reading *any kind of* as one indivisible quantifier. The *of* stands between the two nouns the Hebrew writes.
Nomen rectum takes the construct relation *of* together with its own word, headed on the noun (rules 19, 24).
One connective rendered by a coordinator and a subordinator written together at the recast clause's left edge; headed on the coordinator (rule 55).
Substantival adjective keeps its own word.
The possessive לְ is what makes the verbless clause possessive and carries the *had* (rule 43).
Existential אַיִן heads on the negation word (rule 50).

review_notes: Corrected one edge: the *of* of *for want of clothing* was moved from בְּלִי to its nomen rectum לְבוּשׁ. בְּלִי is tagged Ncmsc here, so a construct relation stands between the two nouns, and rule 19 places that relation on the rectum; the accepted reading treated *want of* as one indivisible English rendering, which rule 19 explicitly forbids for *all of*, *any of* and *any kind of*. Everything else is unchanged.
The privative division follows rule 48: the מִן keeps the function word *for* and the present negative substantive takes the negation word, rather than the מִן taking both.
*the needy had no covering* divides as rule 43 and rule 50 direct — the possessive לְ carries the *had* and אַיִן heads on *no*.
